sounds.hint: Smile a little and hold the sound, like "ee". Your tongue is high and to the front.
A short, relaxed "i". Don't smile as much as in "see" — "sit" is quicker than "seat".
Start with "e" and glide up to "ee": "ay". Let it move, don't keep it flat.
Open your mouth a little more than for "i": a short "eh".
Drop your jaw wide and push your tongue forward: "cat", not "cut".
Open your mouth wide and relax your tongue low, like saying "ah" for a doctor.
A short, relaxed "uh" from the middle of your mouth. Keep your lips loose.
Round your lips a little and open your mouth: "aw".
Start with round lips on "o" and close them more toward "w": "oh-w".
A short "oo" with relaxed lips — "book", not "boot".
Round your lips tightly and hold a long "oo".
Start with an open "ah" and glide to "ee": "eye".
Start with "ah" and close your lips toward "oo": "ow".
Start with round "aw" and glide to "ee": "oy".
The weak "uh" sound. Say it very short and soft — unstressed syllables are quick in English.
Curl your tongue back a little and say "er" without opening wide.
Close your lips, then release with a small puff of air. Hold a paper: it should move.
Close your lips and use your voice — no puff of air.
Touch the ridge behind your top teeth with your tongue tip and release with air.
In American English, "t" between vowels sounds like a quick, soft "d": "wa-der".
Same place as "t", but use your voice: a gentle "d".
Lift the back of your tongue to the roof of your mouth and release with air.
Same place as "k", but use your voice.
Touch your top teeth to your bottom lip and blow air out.
Same as "f" but use your voice — you should feel your lip buzz. Don't use "b".
Put your tongue tip lightly between your teeth and blow air — no voice.
Tongue tip lightly between your teeth, then use your voice. Not "d" or "z".
Keep your teeth close and push air over your tongue tip: a clear hiss.
Same as "s" but with voice — it buzzes. Many plurals end in "z".
Round your lips a little and push air: "sh", like asking for quiet.
Like "sh" but with voice, as in the middle of "measure".
Just breathe out softly from your throat before the vowel. Don't drop it.
Start with "t" and release into "sh" in one quick sound: "ch".
Start with "d" and release into the voiced "zh": "j".
Close your lips and hum through your nose.
Tongue tip behind your top teeth, sound through your nose.
Back of the tongue up, sound through your nose. Don't add a hard "g" at the end.
Touch your tongue tip behind your top teeth and let air flow around the sides.
Pull your tongue back without touching the roof of your mouth. Don't roll or tap it.
Round your lips like "oo", then open quickly. It's not "v".
Start like "ee" and move quickly into the next vowel: the "y" in "yes".
